module_title: Intermediate Grid - Chordata and The Five Vertebrate Classes
introduction: This level targets the subphylum Vertebrata. Questions here heavily focus on matching the class with its heart chambers, blood temperature types (cold vs. warm-blooded), and identifying deceptive mammals.

core_concepts.title: Cold-Blooded vs. Warm-Blooded
core_concepts.description:
- **Poikilotherms (Cold-blooded):** Cannot regulate internal body temperature (it changes with the environment). Includes: Pisces (Fishes), Amphibians, and Reptiles.
- **Homoiotherms (Warm-blooded):** Maintain a constant internal body temperature. Includes: Aves (Birds) and Mammals.

core_concepts.title: Pisces (Fishes) & Amphibians
core_concepts.description:
- **Pisces:** Strictly aquatic. Respire through gills. They possess a **2-chambered heart** (one auricle, one ventricle). Example: Shark, Rohu, Seahorse.
- **Amphibia:** Can live in aquatic and terrestrial habitats. Respire through gills, lungs, or skin. They possess a **3-chambered heart**. Example: Frog, Toad, Salamander.

core_concepts.title: Reptilia & Aves (Birds)
core_concepts.description:
- **Reptilia:** Creeping/crawling mode of locomotion. Covered with dry, cornified skin (scales). Usually have a **3-chambered heart**. Example: Snake, Lizard, Turtle.
- **Aves:** Presence of feathers and a beak. Forelimbs modified into wings. They have hollow (pneumatic) bones to assist in flight and a **4-chambered heart**.

core_concepts.title: Mammalia
core_concepts.description: The defining characteristic of mammals is the presence of **mammary glands** (milk-producing glands) and hair on the skin. They have a **4-chambered heart** and respire through lungs. Most give birth to live young (viviparous).

important_entities.name: Crocodile
important_entities.significance: While almost all reptiles have a 3-chambered heart (or 3.5), the **Crocodile** is the grand exception. It has a fully developed **4-chambered heart**, making it a highly repeated question in UPPSC and SSC.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation:
These are the ultimate biological misdirections used by examiners:
- **Whales & Dolphins:** They live in water and look like giant fish, but they are aquatic **Mammals** (they breathe through lungs/blowholes and give birth to live young).
- **Bat:** It flies like a bird, but it is a flying **Mammal** (produces milk and has hair).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: As evolution progresses from water to land to air/advanced mammals, the heart chambers upgrade: Pisces (2) -> Amphibians/Reptiles (3) -> Aves/Mammals (4).

exam_strategy_tips: Always remember that a Seahorse is a TRUE fish (Pisces), while a Jellyfish is not. Expect questions asking 'Which of the following is warm-blooded?' where the answer is usually a bird (e.g., Ostrich, Penguin) or a mammal (Bat, Whale).
